body: Can't quite verify this claim now but this sentence also exists in AABB and should be removed accordingly.

> Removed "Although [Rect2] itself is axis-aligned, it can be combined with [Transform2D] to represent a rotated or skewed rectangle." because it's misleading.
> 
> What is being transformed are the A and B points. Resulting into a new axis aligned rectangle with the two points being transformed. It's not the rotated rectangle, but the "bounding box" that you obtain.

Well, the thing is you seem to assume that _"Rect2 combined with Transform2D"_ means `Transform2D * Rect2` multiplication. For such interpretation you're indeed correct, the result is given Rect2's axis-aligned bounding rect but within the transform's parent frame.

However _"Rect2 combined with Transform2D"_ can be interpreted differently. E.g. within the RenderingServer rect drawing commands (`CommandRect`) store the local `Rect2` (so an axis-aligned rect), and then its "combined" with the given canvas item's transform to produce the final quad vertices, and such quad can be rotated / non-axis-aligned.
And the same when using `CanvasItem.draw_rect` combined with `CanvasItem`'s own transform (or `CanvasItem.draw_set_custom_transform`).

So overall the in-docs sentence is not totally wrong, but indeed it's unclear and potentially misleading (depending on how it's interpreted). Thus makes sense to remove it.

PS It's me who suggested adding this note in the first place: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/69816#discussion_r1279845318. 🙃
